Building on the operator approach of "A. Itkin, Pricing derivatives under Levy models. Modern finite difference and pseudo-differential operators approach, Springer, 2017, ISBN 978-1-4939-6792-6", we introduce a family of "Diagonal Frog" discretizations whose spatial operators are eventually M-matrices (EM-matrices). Although these operators lack a local M-matrix structure, positivity of the directional sub-operators emerges in the spirit of Zeno's paradox: the matrix exponential, assembled as the limit of infinitely many ever-smaller substeps, is provably nonnegative after a short transient even though no single substep is. For the mixed-derivative block, whose generator is not eventually nonnegative, positivity instead rests on a factorized resolvent solver and holds conditionally, on an explicit step-size window; discrete mass is conserved exactly by the splitting for every step size. The resulting schemes are second-order accurate in time and space and require O(m 2 N + m 3) operations per time step, where m is the dimension of the Krylov subspace used to apply the exponential. As stress tests, we solve a two-dimensional anisotropic Fokker-Planck equation in the strong cross-diffusion regime against an exact Gaussian reference, a Kramers escape problem in a double-well potential, and an advection-dominated problem, and observe that the schemes remain stable, nonnegative, and mass-conservative for a wide range of P\'ecklet numbers (so, don't need any flux limiter). Finally, we extend the construction to multidimensional processes and to the backward Kolmogorov equation with jumps.
tldr: This paper develops high-order positivity-preserving finite difference schemes for anisotropic Fokker-Planck equations using operator splitting and matrix exponentials.
motivation: Standard discretizations of Fokker-Planck equations with cross-diffusion often produce negative probability densities, which is unphysical. The author aims to construct schemes that guarantee nonnegative solutions while maintaining accuracy and efficiency.
method: The 'Diagonal Frog' family of discretizations uses spatial operators that are eventually M-matrices, combined with a factorized resolvent solver for mixed-derivative blocks. The matrix exponential is approximated via Krylov subspace methods, and the scheme is second-order accurate in time and space.
result: The schemes are proven to be positivity-preserving after a short transient and conditionally for mixed derivatives, with exact mass conservation. Numerical tests on 2D anisotropic Fokker-Planck, Kramers escape, and advection-dominated problems show stability, nonnegativity, and mass conservation for a wide range of Péclet numbers.
conclusion: The proposed Diagonal Frog schemes provide a robust numerical method for solving Fokker-Planck equations with anisotropic diffusion, ensuring physical positivity and mass conservation without flux limiters.

title: (Generalized) Spine Subalgebras Of Fourier-Stieltjes Algebras And Their Homomorphisms
authors: Nico Spronk, Ross Stokke, Aasaimani Thamizhazhagan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For any upper semilattice [MATH] of locally precompact topologies on a locally compact group [MATH], we define an associated generalized spine subalgebra [MATH] of the Fourier-Stieltjes algebra [MATH]. We show that [MATH] is a semilattice-graded [MATH]-direct sum of maximal copies of Fourier algebras and we identify its spectrum as a semilattice of groups. We build a collection of examples of generalized spine algebras over whose spectra we exhibit fine control. We define notions of compatible fusions of homomorphisms and affine maps, and use these definitions to characterize all completely positive, completely contractive and, when [MATH] is amenable, all completely bounded homomorphisms from a generalized spine algebra [MATH] to a Fourier-Stieltjes algebra [MATH]. These results are new, even when [MATH] is the full spine algebra [MATH] and even when [MATH] and [MATH] are abelian. We provide examples illustrating the scope of our theorems.
tldr: This paper studies generalized spine subalgebras of Fourier-Stieltjes algebras on locally compact groups and their homomorphisms.
motivation: To understand the structure and homomorphisms of certain subalgebras of Fourier-Stieltjes algebras, which are objects in abstract harmonic analysis.
method: The authors define generalized spine subalgebras using semilattices of topologies, show they are semilattice-graded direct sums, and characterize completely positive, completely contractive, and completely bounded homomorphisms.
result: They identify the spectrum as a semilattice of groups and provide a characterization of homomorphisms in terms of compatible fusions and affine maps.
conclusion: The results are new even for the full spine algebra and for abelian groups, extending the theory of Fourier-Stieltjes algebras.

title: Tractability Versus Curse Of Dimensionality For Geometric $L_p$-discrepancies
authors: Friedrich Pillichshammer Erich Novak
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24195v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies tractability versus the curse of dimensionality for several geometric [MATH]-discrepancies through a unified discrepancy--integration duality framework, where worst case integration errors in suitable function spaces equal the corresponding discrepancies. A general lower bound method for non-negative linear rules in spaces under broad tensor-product assumptions establishes exponential information complexity in the dimension [MATH], yielding the curse of dimensionality for the respective discrepancy. We complement this overview by new results on discrepancy--integration duality and the curse of dimensionality for the periodic [MATH]-discrepancy. The current state of research on this general problem is summarized in a clearly laid out table, which also highlights the remaining open questions.
tldr: This paper studies the curse of dimensionality for geometric Lp-discrepancies using a discrepancy–integration duality framework.
motivation: Understanding whether high-dimensional numerical integration suffers from the curse of dimensionality is a fundamental question in approximation theory.
method: The authors develop a general lower bound method for non-negative linear rules under tensor-product assumptions and apply it to various Lp-discrepancies.
result: They prove exponential information complexity in the dimension for several discrepancies, establishing the curse of dimensionality, and provide new results for the periodic Lp-discrepancy.
conclusion: The paper summarizes the state of research on tractability of geometric discrepancies and highlights open questions.

title: Central Extensions Of Mapping Class Groups Of Surfaces From Stated Skein Algebras
authors: Joris Moulai
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a surface of genus [MATH] with zero or one boundary component and [MATH] marked points, and [MATH] a finite-dimensional factorizable ribbon Hopf algebra. We compute the central extension of the mapping class group of [MATH], associated to the projective representation defined from the stated skein algebra of [MATH] and [MATH]. Our proof is purely two-dimensional, and makes no use of TQFT arguments.
tldr: This paper computes central extensions of mapping class groups from stated skein algebras, a purely mathematical result in low-dimensional topology and representation theory.
motivation: To understand projective representations of mapping class groups arising from skein algebras, which are important in topological quantum field theories.
method: Uses algebraic methods involving stated skein algebras and finite-dimensional factorizable ribbon Hopf algebras, with a purely two-dimensional proof avoiding TQFT.
result: Computes the central extension of the mapping class group associated to the projective representation from the stated skein algebra.
conclusion: Provides a complete algebraic description of the central extension, contributing to the theory of mapping class groups and skein algebras.

title: Discrepancy For Random Linear Codes
authors: Dean Doron, Tal Leonov, Jonathan Mosheiff, Henrique Navas, Nicolas Resch, Jo\~ao Ribeiro
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that random linear codes have nearly optimal discrepancy properties in a broad range of regimes. Our main results are two general theorems: one controlling all translates of a fixed test, and another controlling large families of Fourier-pseudorandom tests. Two motivating applications follow. First, random linear codes match unstructured random codes for list-decoding from errors above capacity. If [MATH] is a random linear code of rate [MATH], where [MATH] is a radius-[MATH] Hamming ball, then with high probability $[MATH][MATH]\rho[MATH]B\subseteq\mathbb F_q^n[MATH]\rho n[MATH]q>2[MATH]2\le \ell\le q-1[MATH]1-\log_q\ell+\epsilon[MATH][MATH][MATH]S=S_1\times\cdots\times S_n[MATH]|S_i|=\ell[MATH]n[MATH]\mathbb F_q[MATH]n/(2\log q)[MATH]5n/(2\log q)[MATH]n/2[MATH]n[MATH]q\le n^{1/5-o(1)}[MATH]C$.
tldr: The paper proves that random linear codes have nearly optimal discrepancy properties, with applications to list-decoding and combinatorial design.
motivation: To understand the discrepancy of random linear codes compared to unstructured random codes, and to derive implications for list-decoding and combinatorial designs.
method: The authors prove two general theorems controlling all translates of a fixed test and large families of Fourier-pseudorandom tests, using probabilistic and combinatorial arguments.
result: Random linear codes match unstructured random codes for list-decoding from errors above capacity, and they achieve optimal discrepancy for Cartesian product sets.
conclusion: Random linear codes exhibit nearly optimal discrepancy in a broad range of regimes, demonstrating their power beyond traditional coding theory.

title: Randomized Estimation Of T-Eigenvalues Of T-spd Tensors: A Two-Sided Bracket
authors: Nachiketa Mishra Hemant Sharma
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In earlier work we developed deterministic analytical bounds on the T-eigenvalues of symmetric positive definite (SPD) third-order tensors under the Kilmer--Martin T-product: the trace--determinant (TDet) bounds via the AM--GM inequality, and the trace-dependent (TDep) bounds generalizing Samuelson's inequality. While these bounds are cheap and guaranteed-valid, their relative gap grows as [MATH] in the tensor dimension [MATH], limiting their usefulness for large tensors. This paper develops randomized estimators for the extreme T-eigenvalues of T-SPD tensors that complement the deterministic bounds. We adapt the Halko--Martinsson--Tropp framework to the T-product setting and introduce four methods: (i) a randomized power method that produces a lower bound on [MATH] with exponential convergence; (ii) a randomized subspace iteration with a tensor-analogue HMT error bound; (iii) a two-sided rigorous bracket combining the randomized lower bound with the deterministic TDep upper bound; and (iv) a Hutchinson-based fully randomized TDep bound for matvec-only settings.
tldr: This paper develops randomized estimators for extreme T-eigenvalues of third-order tensors under the T-product, extending linear algebra techniques to tensor settings.
motivation: Deterministic bounds on T-eigenvalues become loose for large tensors, so randomized methods are needed to provide tighter estimates.
method: Adapts the Halko-Martinsson-Tropp randomized SVD framework to the T-product algebra, introducing a randomized power method, subspace iteration, two-sided bracket, and Hutchinson-based bound.
result: The randomized methods yield lower bounds with exponential convergence and complement deterministic upper bounds, producing rigorous intervals for extreme T-eigenvalues.
conclusion: Randomized estimators offer a practical way to bound T-eigenvalues for large T-SPD tensors where deterministic bounds are too weak.

title: Analysis And Approximation Of A Two-dimensional Induction Heating Problem
authors: Gabriel R. Barrenechea, Katherine Mackenzie, Abner Salgado
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we analyse the existence of solutions and finite element approximation of a steady-state two-dimensional induction heating problem. One of the main difficulties of the problem is its right-hand side which, at a first sight, is only integrable. Using a priori regularity results for the PDEs involved it is shown that the natural weak formulation of the problem can be justified. Then, we study the finite element approximation and prove that the standard Galerkin FEM converges in convex domains and under suitable conditions on the mesh. We improve on this result by applying the recently-proposed bound-preserving method (BPM) to the heat equation, and show that this method converges to a solution of the problem under less stringent conditions on the domain and the mesh. As these analyses are carried out without any assumption on regularity of the solutions, then the convergence of the finite element method also proves existence of solutions. Several numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results, and showcase the improvement provided by the use of the bound-preserving method over the standard finite element method.
tldr: This paper analyzes the existence of solutions and finite element approximation of a steady-state two-dimensional induction heating problem.
motivation: Induction heating is an important industrial process, but its mathematical analysis is challenging due to a right-hand side that is only integrable at first sight.
method: The authors use a priori regularity results for the PDEs to justify the weak formulation, then study standard Galerkin FEM and a bound-preserving method (BPM) for convergence.
result: They prove convergence of the standard FEM under convex domains and suitable mesh conditions, and show that BPM converges under less stringent conditions without regularity assumptions.
conclusion: The finite element method converges to a solution, and the bound-preserving method improves convergence conditions; numerical experiments confirm the theory.

title: Spectrally $n$-centered Operators. I
authors: Piotr Budzy\'nski
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the concept of spectrally [MATH]-centered operators and study it within the framework of unbounded weighted composition operators in [MATH]-spaces. Based on this, we establish a characterisation of spectrally centered unbounded weighted composition operators, generalising Giselsson's criterion to the unbounded regime. Finally, we analyse various associated conditions, highlighting the delicate measure-theoretic anomalies.
tldr: Introduces spectrally n-centered operators and characterizes them for unbounded weighted composition operators on L^p-spaces.
motivation: To generalize the concept of centered operators to the spectral setting and extend Giselsson's criterion to unbounded operators.
method: Develops the theory of spectrally n-centered operators and applies it to unbounded weighted composition operators using measure-theoretic analysis.
result: Provides a characterization of spectrally centered unbounded weighted composition operators, highlighting measure-theoretic anomalies.
conclusion: The work establishes a foundation for spectrally centered operators in the unbounded regime, with implications for operator theory.

title: Norm Of Infinite Doubly Stochastic Matrices
authors: Ludovick Bouthat, Javad Mashreghi, Rapha\"el Vo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In finite dimensions, every doubly stochastic matrix has the [MATH]-operator norm equal to [MATH] for all [MATH]. However, in the infinite-dimensional setting, this property may fail since the norm can be strictly smaller than [MATH] when [MATH]. In this paper, a complete characterization of infinite doubly stochastic matrices for which the norm remains equal to [MATH] is obtained. More precisely, for [MATH], it is shown that $[MATH][MATH]\Theta[MATH]1$ precisely when the matrix contains arbitrarily large finite regions in which it behaves almost like a finite doubly stochastic matrix. The proof uses a Cheeger-type argument, highlighting a natural connection with ideas from spectral graph theory.
tldr: Characterizes infinite doubly stochastic matrices whose operator norm equals 1.
motivation: To understand when the norm property of finite doubly stochastic matrices extends to infinite dimensions.
method: Uses a Cheeger-type argument from spectral graph theory to analyze the norm of infinite doubly stochastic matrices.
result: The norm equals 1 if and only if the matrix contains arbitrarily large finite regions that behave almost like finite doubly stochastic matrices.
conclusion: The norm condition is equivalent to a certain asymptotic stochasticity property, linking infinite matrix theory to spectral graph theory.

title: Rationalizing Collective Revealed Preferences With An Application In Fair Resource Allocation
authors: Chuwen Zhang, Zhiyun Guo, Zizhuo Wang, Yinyu Ye
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a revealed preference approach for rationalizing collective consumption behavior. We introduce the Constructive Rationalization Method (CRM), which approximates the real market via a surrogate market of artificial consumers, called androids, with easy-to-compute demand functions. CRM uses observed aggregate demand and adds artificial consumers on the fly, while redistributing wealth under an empirical risk minimization principle. Unlike classical revealed preference approaches, CRM provides guarantees on the generalization risk for learning the aggregate demand function, while respecting the privacy of the underlying consumers in the real market. As an application, CRM can be used to provide reliable predictions for collective consumption behavior. Specifically, we show how to apply CRM to approximate allocations that are proportionally fair without requiring the knowledge of individual utilities.
tldr: This paper presents a revealed preference approach for rationalizing collective consumption behavior using artificial consumers, with an application to fair resource allocation.
motivation: Classical revealed preference approaches lack guarantees on generalization risk and privacy. The authors aim to provide a method that learns aggregate demand functions while preserving individual privacy.
method: The Constructive Rationalization Method (CRM) approximates the real market by introducing artificial consumers (androids) with easy-to-compute demand functions, using empirical risk minimization to redistribute wealth.
result: CRM provides guarantees on generalization risk for learning aggregate demand and can approximate proportionally fair allocations without knowledge of individual utilities.
conclusion: CRM offers a privacy-preserving, data-driven approach to rationalize collective consumption and predict fair resource allocations.

title: Token Complexity Of Certifying Stochastic-Oracle Reliability
authors: Jie Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wang~ introduced the Stochastic-Oracle Turing Machine (SOTM) framework and defined token complexity as the minimum expected cost of interacting with a stochastic oracle needed to attain a specified solution quality for a task. This paper develops an analogous notion for certifying the reliability of a stochastic oracle on a given domain. Certification token complexity is the minimum expected token cost required, with controlled error probability, to distinguish oracles that meet a target reliability level from those that fall below a lower reliability threshold. We construct an SPRT-based certification SOTM that queries the oracle, computes binary correctness scores, and stops when the accumulated log-likelihood evidence crosses a decision threshold. The SOTM halts almost surely, satisfies the desired two-sided error guarantee over the reliability regions to be certified, and yields an explicit upper bound on certification token complexity in terms of the reliability thresholds, the error bound, and the expected per-turn token cost. We then establish a matching information-theoretic lower bound: even with adaptive queries, every error-bounded certification SOTM must incur the same leading-order expected token cost as the SPRT-based construction as the prescribed error bound tends to zero. Together, these bounds characterize the leading-order certification token complexity in the small-error regime.
tldr: This paper introduces a token complexity framework for certifying the reliability of stochastic oracles using SPRT-based Turing machines.
motivation: To develop a rigorous measure of the expected cost (token complexity) required to certify whether a stochastic oracle meets a reliability threshold, with controlled error probability.
method: Constructs an SPRT-based certification Stochastic-Oracle Turing Machine (SOTM) that queries the oracle and stops when accumulated log-likelihood evidence crosses a decision threshold, and derives matching information-theoretic lower bounds.
result: Provides explicit upper and lower bounds on certification token complexity in the small-error regime, showing the SPRT-based construction is asymptotically optimal.
conclusion: The leading-order certification token complexity is characterized by the reliability thresholds, error bound, and expected per-turn token cost, with the SPRT-based SOTM achieving optimal performance.

title: Exact Schur-Sylvester Dimensionality Reductions For Non-Smooth Stochastic Complexity And Manifold Sampling
authors: Gary P. T. Choi Trenton Lau
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23867v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The exact computation of the Normalized Maximum Likelihood (NML) codelength for regular non-smooth estimators (e.g., Lasso) has been historically limited by the cubic scaling walls of manifold-constrained projection and volume integration. At each step of the geometric Propose-and-Project Metropolis--Hastings (PPMH) sampler, evaluating the projection operator requires inverting an [MATH] generalized KKT matrix, while calculating the volume factor requires the determinant of an [MATH] Gram matrix. This paper presents an exact, mathematically equivalent formulation that bypasses both bottlenecks by utilizing the block Schur complement and Sylvester's determinant identity. We prove that the computational complexity of both operations collapses from [MATH] to [MATH] per step. We generalize this reduction to Sparse Support Vector Machines (SVMs), Elastic Net, and Group Lasso. Finally, we provide a rigorous numerical stability analysis and evaluate the sampler's efficiency using the Effective Sample Size (ESS) per second. Our empirical benchmarks on high-dimensional datasets confirm a constant speedup exceeding [MATH] while maintaining double-precision numerical equivalence, rendering exact non-smooth NML estimation highly tractable for large-scale statistical inference.
tldr: This paper presents exact Schur-Sylvester dimensionality reductions to accelerate the computation of Normalized Maximum Likelihood codelength for non-smooth estimators like Lasso, using a Propose-and-Project Metropolis-Hastings sampler.
motivation: Exact NML computation for non-smooth estimators is computationally prohibitive due to cubic scaling of projection and volume integration steps.
method: The authors reformulate the projection operator and volume factor using block Schur complement and Sylvester's determinant identity, reducing complexity from O(n^3) to O(n^2) per step.
result: The method achieves a constant speedup exceeding 10x while maintaining double-precision numerical equivalence, demonstrated on high-dimensional datasets.
conclusion: The proposed reductions make exact non-smooth NML estimation tractable for large-scale statistical inference.

title: The Serialized Bridge: Understanding And Recovering Llm Serving Performance Under Blackwell Gpu Confidential Computing
authors: Kevin Wang Hang Yin
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23969v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: GPU Confidential Computing (GPU-CC) now preserves GPU-local performance: on NVIDIA B300, BF16 matmul runs at 0.998x of non-confidential performance. Yet LLM serving under Intel TDX plus GPU-CC still loses 13-27% of throughput, and KV-cache restore latency can more than double. This paper studies that gap on two Blackwell platforms, RTX Pro 6000 and B300 HGX, and identifies its dominant cause: the confidential VM-GPU bridge, not GPU compute. We find that GPU-CC turns host/device movement into a serialized, high-setup-cost channel. Secure copies do not gain CUDA-stream concurrency within a context, asynchronous transfers block at the runtime boundary, and small crossings pay a fixed toll. This violates the assumptions of modern inference runtimes, where DMA is expected to be cheap, concurrent, and asynchronous. In vLLM dense decode, the gap closes around 44x-slower small alloc-and-copy operations; targeted patches reject alternative explanations. A scheduling flag recovers 57% of the gap, while a worker-thread drain recovers up to 92% in qualified high-concurrency runs. The same bridge model explains a +131% KV-restore penalty and a 34x model-load slowdown. Blackwell also changes the confidential tenancy unit. We qualify confidential multi-GPU NVSwitch tenants on B300, including 510 GB/s NVLink P2P inside a CVM and concurrent isolated tenants, and identify the remaining fabric-attestation gap for production confidential AI platforms.
tldr: This paper analyzes performance degradation in LLM serving under GPU confidential computing on Blackwell platforms, identifying the serialized VM-GPU bridge as the main bottleneck.
motivation: GPU confidential computing preserves local GPU performance, but LLM serving still suffers significant throughput loss; the paper aims to identify and recover this gap.
method: The authors profile two Blackwell platforms (RTX Pro 6000 and B300 HGX), measure performance under Intel TDX plus GPU-CC, and isolate the cause via targeted patches and scheduling changes.
result: The confidential VM-GPU bridge serializes host/device movement, causing 13-27% throughput loss and up to 2x KV-cache restore latency; a scheduling flag recovers 57% of the gap, and a worker-thread drain recovers up to 92%.
conclusion: The main performance bottleneck is the serialized bridge, not GPU compute; the findings suggest improvements for confidential AI platforms.

title: Broadband And Flat-baseline Dual-comb Cavity Mode Dispersion Spectroscopy Using Fiber-based Frequency Combs
authors: Sho Okubo, Ken Kashiwagi, Koji Hashiguchi, Hajime Inaba
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate broadband dual-comb cavity mode dispersion spectroscopy using mode-locked erbium-fiber frequency combs and a length-tunable optical cavity. The flat baseline and low-noise characteristics of cavity-mode-dispersion spectroscopy, combined with the broadband coverage of fiber frequency combs, provide highly precise spectral profiles that are difficult to obtain with conventional dual-comb spectroscopy. We measured the entire [MATH] band of acetylene in the [MATH] region. The simultaneous fitting of multiple transitions agreed well with the measured spectra, yielding a relative standard deviation of 0.27 % for the retrieved acetylene pressure and a spectral fluctuation corresponding to an absorption coefficient of [MATH]. These results reveal the high precision achievable with the present method. Further sensitivity improvements are expected with a higher-finesse cavity.
tldr: This paper demonstrates broadband dual-comb cavity mode dispersion spectroscopy using fiber-based frequency combs for high-precision molecular spectroscopy.
motivation: To achieve highly precise spectral profiles with flat baseline and low noise, overcoming limitations of conventional dual-comb spectroscopy.
method: Uses mode-locked erbium-fiber frequency combs and a length-tunable optical cavity to perform cavity-mode-dispersion spectroscopy across a broad bandwidth.
result: Measured the entire ν1+ν3 band of acetylene with high precision, yielding a relative standard deviation of 0.27% for pressure and spectral fluctuation corresponding to an absorption coefficient of 5.0×10⁻⁹ cm⁻¹.
conclusion: The method provides high precision and further sensitivity improvements are expected with a higher-finesse cavity.

title: Regimes Of Influence In Trust-Uncertainty Gated Networks
authors: Razieh Masoumi, Ahana Biswas, Yu-Ru Lin
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In many social communities, individuals can simultaneously trust and distrust the same source, a feature standard opinion-dynamics models often ignore. We formalize this ambivalence with Gated Network Credence, in which each directed relationship encodes distinct trust and distrust assessments. These jointly determine "net trust" - the willingness to rely on a source - and "uncertainty" - the conflict between trust and distrust within the same relationship. Agents update beliefs only when net trust exceeds a threshold and uncertainty falls below another, yielding an effective influence graph whose topology drives long-run belief states. Sweeping both thresholds uncovers four regimes - Pluralistic, Selective, Concordant, and Fortified - that differ in openness to trust and conflict. We find a consistent hub-periphery reversal: in the Selective regime, high-degree agents dominate influence, whereas in the Concordant regime, stringent uncertainty filtering disproportionately removes active influence channels associated with high-degree agents, enabling peripheral lower-degree agents to exert greater leverage over the collective equilibrium. This reversal holds across synthetic and empirical networks. Our results show that belief dynamics depend not only on network structure but also on how relational ambivalence between trust and distrust gates interpersonal influence.
tldr: This paper studies opinion dynamics in social networks where trust and distrust are modeled separately, leading to different influence regimes.
motivation: Standard opinion-dynamics models ignore the simultaneous presence of trust and distrust in relationships, which can affect how beliefs spread.
method: The authors introduce a Gated Network Credence model where agents update beliefs based on net trust and uncertainty thresholds, and they analyze the resulting influence graph topology across synthetic and empirical networks.
result: They identify four regimes (Pluralistic, Selective, Concordant, Fortified) and observe a hub-periphery reversal where stringent uncertainty filtering can empower low-degree agents.
conclusion: Belief dynamics depend not only on network structure but also on how relational ambivalence gates interpersonal influence.

title: Exact Vs Approximate Second-order Derivatives In Vertically-integrated Ice Sheet Models
authors: Stephen L. Cornford Trystan Surawy-Stepney
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Second order derivatives of model outputs with respect to input parameters are key to several applications in ice sheet modelling. For example, the ability to compute Hessian-vector products broadens the list of available optimisation methods, and facilitates certain kinds of parametric uncertainty quantification. Some modern ice sheet models are built on frameworks supporting algorithmic differentiation (AD), allowing for the computation of higher order derivatives with relative ease. However, many of our most widely-used models are not. A natural alternative might be to follow common practise in first order gradient computation and construct an approximate second-order adjoint model at the PDE level, which neglects the nonlinear dependence of ice viscosity on velocity. Here, we present such a model for the shallow-stream approximation allowing one to compute approximate second-order derivatives, and compare with full second-order derivates found using AD. We find that this produces Hessian-vector products that are superficially similar to those computed via AD. However, an analysis of the spectral decomposition of the Hessians calculated in each way reveals that the subspaces spanned by their eigenvectors diverge after the leading 4 modes, though divergence does not accelerate after this. We conclude that the utility of the approximate Hessian is case-dependent, and a full Hessian, likely computed using AD, should be used where high fidelity is required above very low rank.
tldr: This paper compares exact and approximate second-order derivatives in ice sheet models, focusing on Hessian-vector products for optimization and uncertainty quantification.
motivation: Second-order derivatives are needed for optimization and uncertainty quantification in ice sheet modeling, but many models lack algorithmic differentiation support, motivating approximate methods.
method: The authors develop an approximate second-order adjoint model for the shallow-stream approximation that neglects nonlinear viscosity dependence, and compare it with exact derivatives computed via algorithmic differentiation.
result: Approximate Hessian-vector products are superficially similar to exact ones, but spectral analysis shows eigenvectors diverge after the first 4 modes, though divergence does not accelerate.
conclusion: The utility of the approximate Hessian is case-dependent; full Hessian computed via AD is recommended when high fidelity beyond very low rank is required.

title: Low-Complexity Hybrid Precoding For Cell-Free Massive Mu-mimo Isac Systems
authors: Jun Zhu, Yin Xu, Aimin Tang, Ruomeng Wang, Dazhi He, Yunfeng Guan, Wenjun Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in cell-free (CF) massive multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) system is a promising architecture for high-rate communications and high-accuracy multi-target sensing. However, centralized coordination among distributed access points (APs) incurs substantial fronthaul overhead and computation complexity. This paper proposes a low-complexity hybrid precoding framework for CF massive MU-MIMO ISAC systems with partially-connected architectures at the APs. By applying hybrid architecture at the APs, the proposed framework converts the original high-dimensional channel information into a low-dimensional effective channel, enabling digital precoding over the compressed channel domain and thereby substantially reducing both fronthaul overhead and baseband computational complexity. We formulate the joint hybrid precoding design as an ergodic sum-rate (ESR) maximization problem with position error bound (PEB) constraints to ensure multi-target sensing accuracy. An efficient alternating optimization (AO)-based solver is then developed, where the PEB constraint is reformulated into tractable convex constraints, while the digital-domain optimization is carried out over the reduced-dimensional effective channel and the analog precoding is refined on the constant-modulus manifold. For dynamic user topology, we further propose multi-branch (MB) rate-splitting (RS) minimum mean-square-error Tomlinson-Harashima precoding (MMSE-THP) update algorithm that combines multi-branch ordering with recursive MMSE-THP matrix updates, enabling common and private digital precodings to be refreshed without repeated full matrix recomputation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves high ESR and accurate multi-target sensing while reducing computational complexity by 87.02\% compared with conventional baselines.
tldr: This paper proposes a low-complexity hybrid precoding framework for cell-free massive MU-MIMO ISAC systems, focusing on reducing fronthaul overhead and computational complexity.
motivation: Centralized coordination in cell-free massive MIMO ISAC systems incurs high fronthaul overhead and computational complexity, which this work aims to reduce.
method: The authors apply hybrid precoding with partially-connected architectures, formulate an ergodic sum-rate maximization with PEB constraints, and develop an alternating optimization solver with multi-branch rate-splitting MMSE-THP updates.
result: The proposed scheme achieves high ergodic sum-rate and accurate multi-target sensing while reducing computational complexity by 87.02% compared to conventional baselines.
conclusion: The hybrid precoding framework effectively balances communication and sensing performance with significantly lower complexity, making it suitable for practical cell-free ISAC systems.

title: Characterization Of Paired And Toeplitz + Hankel Operators On The Polydisc
authors: Kritika Babbar, Mo Javed, Amit Maji
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we obtain a complete classification of Toeplitz + Hankel operators on the vector-valued Hardy space [MATH] over the polydisc [MATH] in [MATH] for [MATH]. We also characterize the paired operators on [MATH]. For an inner function [MATH], we further characterize [MATH]-paired operators on [MATH] with respect to the Beurling submodule [MATH].
tldr: This paper classifies Toeplitz+Hankel and paired operators on vector-valued Hardy spaces over the polydisc, a topic in pure functional analysis.
motivation: To extend the classification of Toeplitz+Hankel operators from the unit disc to the polydisc and characterize paired operators with respect to Beurling submodules.
method: Uses operator theory on Hardy spaces over the polydisc, analyzing Toeplitz+Hankel and paired operators via function-theoretic and algebraic techniques.
result: Provides a complete classification of Toeplitz+Hankel operators on vector-valued Hardy spaces over the polydisc and characterizes paired operators and inner-function-paired operators.
conclusion: The classification results generalize known results from the unit disc to the polydisc, contributing to operator theory on several complex variables.

title: Computational Framework For B\'ezier Distributions
authors: Esteban Leiva, Andr\'es L. Medaglia, Luis F. Zuluaga
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Flexible continuous univariate distributions with bounded support are essential for accurate input modeling in stochastic simulation and decision analysis. Although B\'ezier distributions provide a powerful family capable of representing complex shapes, their adoption has been hindered by the lack of efficient fitting procedures and modern software implementations. This paper develops a computational framework for fitting B\'ezier distributions to empirical data via both minimum error and maximum likelihood estimation, leveraging first-order optimization methods and exploiting the geometry of the parameter space. We identify provably (asymptotically) lossless convex restrictions of the feasible set that enable efficient projection operators based on isotonic regression and develop first-order algorithms that reduce computational runtime by three to four orders of magnitude compared to traditional derivative-free methods, while delivering consistent fits across real-world data. When benchmarked against the nonlinear solver IPOPT, our methods prove three orders of magnitude faster on average and more robust, while achieving comparable accuracy. To bridge the gap between theory and practice, we introduce bezierv, an open-source Python package providing a unified interface for fitting, analyzing, and convolving B\'ezier distributions.
tldr: This paper presents a computational framework for fitting Bézier distributions to empirical data using first-order optimization methods.
motivation: Bézier distributions are flexible for modeling bounded data but lack efficient fitting procedures and software implementations.
method: The authors develop minimum error and maximum likelihood estimation using first-order optimization with convex restrictions and isotonic regression-based projection operators.
result: The proposed methods reduce computational runtime by three to four orders of magnitude compared to traditional derivative-free methods and are more robust than IPOPT.
conclusion: The framework enables practical use of Bézier distributions, supported by an open-source Python package.

title: On The Geometry Of Unbounded Wandering Domains
authors: Beno U\v{c}akar
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the geometry of unbounded wandering domains of entire functions using Arakelian approximation. First, we show that, given a uniformly accessible closed set contained in a strip, the connected components of its interior can be realized as escaping or oscillating wandering domains of some entire function. The iterates of the function are univalent on these wandering domains, and any unbounded wandering domain remains unbounded under iteration. Second, we show that, in some precise sense, any simply connected open set can be approximated by escaping or oscillating wandering domains. As a direct consequence, we obtain wandering domains whose complements have arbitrarily small areas.
tldr: This paper studies the geometry of unbounded wandering domains of entire functions using Arakelian approximation.
motivation: To understand the possible shapes and properties of wandering domains in complex dynamics.
method: Uses Arakelian approximation theory to construct entire functions with prescribed wandering domains.
result: Shows that any uniformly accessible closed set in a strip can be realized as a wandering domain, and any simply connected open set can be approximated by wandering domains.
conclusion: Wandering domains can have very general geometries, including complements of arbitrarily small area.

title: A Periodic Flow With High Emergence
authors: Odylo Costa
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a smooth nonsingular periodic flow on a compact manifold with high emergence, in sharp contrast with the low statistical complexity of periodic self-maps. The construction is based on a modification of the Epstein--Vogt counterexample to the Periodic Orbit Conjecture and on the high-emergence mechanism of Berger--Bochi.
tldr: This paper constructs a smooth periodic flow on a compact manifold with high emergence, a concept from dynamical systems theory.
motivation: To demonstrate that periodic flows can exhibit high complexity (emergence), contrary to the low complexity of periodic self-maps.
method: The construction modifies the Epstein–Vogt counterexample to the Periodic Orbit Conjecture and incorporates the high-emergence mechanism of Berger–Bochi.
result: A smooth nonsingular periodic flow on a compact manifold with high emergence is obtained.
conclusion: Periodic flows can have high statistical complexity, challenging previous intuitions about periodic dynamics.

title: Order Restricted Estimation Of The Parameter Functions In An Additive Hazard Model
authors: Elbatoul Manel Merai Dragi Anevski
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we propose estimators of the parameter functions in an Aalen additive hasard regression model. The estimators are the individual and componentwise [MATH] projections of the naive estimators resulting from the ordinary least squares estimator in the Aalen additive hazard model on the space of monotone functions. We provide pointwise limit distribution results for the resulting estimators, that exhibit [MATH] rate of convergence and the Chernoff distribution as the limit distribution.
tldr: This paper proposes estimators for parameter functions in an Aalen additive hazard regression model using isotonic regression, with pointwise limit distribution results.
motivation: To estimate monotone parameter functions in survival analysis under an additive hazard model, improving upon naive least squares estimators.
method: The estimators are obtained by projecting naive ordinary least squares estimators onto the space of monotone functions using isotonic regression.
result: The resulting estimators achieve a cube-root rate of convergence and follow a Chernoff distribution in the limit.
conclusion: The proposed method provides consistent estimation of monotone parameter functions in additive hazard models with known asymptotic distribution.

title: Constrained Variable Projection For Structured Problems
authors: Emanuele Zangrando, Sara Venturini, Francesco Rinaldi, Francesco Tudisco
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23939v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Variable projection is a classical technique for separable nonlinear least-squares problems, in which variables that enter linearly are eliminated exactly, yielding a reduced nonlinear problem. By expressing this framework as a particular instance of a broader class of bilevel optimization problems, we develop a constrained variable-projection framework for data-science models, where the remaining variables are subject to convex constraints and the eliminated variables arise from a lower-level least-squares problem. In particular, by interpreting variable projection as a collapsed bilevel optimization problem, we derive exact reduced-gradient formulas compatible with automatic differentiation and propose a conditional-gradient algorithm for the resulting constrained reduced problem. We establish convergence guarantees under standard smoothness and compactness assumptions, and discuss extensions to structured lower-level variables. Numerical experiments on sparse autoencoding, dictionary learning, blind deconvolution, and few-shot learning suggest that the method can improve wall-clock efficiency and data efficiency relative to natural joint-optimization baselines.
tldr: This paper presents a constrained variable projection method for structured optimization problems in data science, with applications to sparse autoencoding and dictionary learning.
motivation: Variable projection is a classical technique for separable nonlinear least-squares problems, but existing methods do not handle convex constraints on the nonlinear variables or structured lower-level problems.
method: The authors reformulate variable projection as a bilevel optimization problem, derive exact reduced gradients compatible with automatic differentiation, and propose a conditional gradient algorithm for the constrained reduced problem.
result: Convergence guarantees are established under standard assumptions, and numerical experiments on sparse autoencoding, dictionary learning, blind deconvolution, and few-shot learning show improved wall-clock and data efficiency compared to joint optimization baselines.
conclusion: The constrained variable projection framework provides an efficient and theoretically grounded approach for structured data-science models, with potential for broader applications.

title: A Lorentzian Lasry-Lions Regularization Theorem
authors: Alec Metsch
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The main goal of this paper is to establish a general Lorentzian Lasry-Lions regularization theorem: let [MATH] be a function defined on a globally hyperbolic spacetime. Assume that its forward Lax--Oleinik evolution [MATH] is locally semiconcave in a neighbourhood of [MATH] and has future-directed timelike superdifferentials there. Then, for [MATH] close to [MATH] and sufficiently small [MATH], the function [MATH] is of class [MATH] in a neighbourhood of [MATH]. We give sufficient conditions ensuring the assumptions of the theorem and present an application to optimal transport: under quite general assumptions, for any two intermediate measures along a displacement interpolation, there exists a [MATH]-regular maximizing pair in the dual formulation.
tldr: This paper proves a Lorentzian Lasry-Lions regularization theorem for functions on globally hyperbolic spacetimes, with an application to optimal transport.
motivation: To establish regularity properties of functions in Lorentzian geometry, which are useful for optimal transport on spacetimes.
method: The paper uses Lax-Oleinik evolution and semiconcavity assumptions to derive C^{1,1} regularity via a Lorentzian adaptation of the Lasry-Lions regularization technique.
result: Under certain conditions, the forward Lax-Oleinik evolution of a function becomes C^{1,1} in a neighborhood, and this is applied to show existence of a C^{1,1} maximizing pair in displacement interpolation.
conclusion: The theorem provides a Lorentzian analogue of a classical regularization result, with implications for optimal transport in curved spacetimes.

title: Computing The Minimal Monomial Basis For Multivariate Birkhoff Interpolation
authors: Li Yuanhe, Jiang Xue, Li Zhe
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies algorithms for computing the minimal monomial basis for multivariate Birkhoff interpolation problems. Our approach is built around the notion of a reverse reduced set, which serves as the key tool for bridging the interpolation conditions to the monomial basis, thereby avoiding the construction and evaluation of Vandermonde matrices required in existing algorithms. For the single-node case, we prove that after Gaussian elimination on the incidence matrix, the least monomials of the polynomial set corresponding to the interpolation conditions precisely constitute the minimal monomial basis. To handle the multi-node case, we exploit the one-to-one correspondence between interpolation functionals and formal power series, whereby interpolation conditions at arbitrary nonzero nodes can all be converted to the origin. This provides both a coherent theoretical framework and a constructive algorithm for determining a proper minimal monomial basis for the general multivariate Birkhoff interpolation problem. Numerical examples demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.
tldr: This paper presents algorithms for computing minimal monomial bases for multivariate Birkhoff interpolation problems.
motivation: Existing algorithms require constructing and evaluating Vandermonde matrices, which is computationally expensive. The authors aim to provide a more efficient approach.
method: The method uses a reverse reduced set to bridge interpolation conditions to monomial basis, and converts multi-node cases to the origin via formal power series.
result: The algorithm avoids Vandermonde matrices and is demonstrated to be effective on numerical examples.
conclusion: The proposed algorithm provides a coherent theoretical framework and constructive method for multivariate Birkhoff interpolation.

title: E Scheme And Flux-Limiter Scheme, Revisited
authors: Huazhong Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper revisits the {\em E scheme} of Osher and the {\em flux-limiter scheme} of Sweby for quasi-linear hyperbolic conservation laws . Part of existing results will be re-understood and some new results will be presented. For a scalar conservation law, except for the conservative monotone schemes, the E scheme is a type of numerical methods that satisfy the discrete entropy condition for any convex entropy, but numerical entropy flux is not unique. Two-point E flux is monotone flux, but multi-point (three or more points) E flux may not necessarily be monotone flux, and multi-point monotone flux may not necessarily be E flux. Sweby's flux-limiter scheme for the quasi-linear conservation laws was built on the E flux-based splitting [MATH] and the LW scheme. It may not be second-order accurate in both space and time.
tldr: This paper revisits numerical schemes for hyperbolic conservation laws, focusing on E schemes and flux-limiter schemes.
motivation: To re-understand existing results and present new findings on the properties of E schemes and flux-limiter schemes for quasi-linear hyperbolic conservation laws.
method: Theoretical analysis of numerical schemes, including monotonicity, entropy conditions, and accuracy order.
result: Two-point E flux is monotone, but multi-point E flux may not be; multi-point monotone flux may not be E flux. Sweby's flux-limiter scheme may not be second-order accurate.
conclusion: The paper clarifies the relationship between E schemes and monotone schemes, and highlights limitations of the flux-limiter scheme.

title: Quasi-Monte Carlo For Sde Simulation: Error Analysis And Dimensionality Reduction
authors: Du Ouyang, Zexin Pan, Zhijian He
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24207v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the numerical simulation of general stochastic differential equations (SDEs) using Quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) methods. First, we provide a rigorous theoretical analysis of the QMC method applied to the Euler-Maruyama (EM) scheme, establishing that it significantly accelerates the decay of the sampling error and achieves an asymptotically superior convergence rate over the classical Monte Carlo method. Second, the traditional EM scheme exhibits a slow polynomial decay of the discretization error, which necessitates a large number of time steps and leads to a significantly high integration dimension. To address this issue, we propose a Multilevel Stochastic Time Grid (MSTG) method based on Exact Simulation techniques, and we rigorously establish its convergence rate under randomized QMC sampling, proving that it preserves the high-order convergence of the sampling error. In terms of the overall error, the truncation error of the proposed MSTG method exhibits a remarkably fast super-exponential decay. Consequently, to achieve a given accuracy level, our approach requires significantly fewer discretization steps than the EM scheme, thereby drastically reducing the actual integration dimension of the QMC method. This substantial dimensionality reduction strategy greatly enhances the practical efficiency of the QMC algorithm. Numerical experiments fully corroborate the superiority of the proposed approach.
tldr: This paper analyzes Quasi-Monte Carlo methods for stochastic differential equation simulation, focusing on error analysis and dimensionality reduction.
motivation: To improve the efficiency of numerical simulation of SDEs by accelerating convergence and reducing effective dimension.
method: The authors provide theoretical analysis of QMC for Euler-Maruyama scheme and propose a Multilevel Stochastic Time Grid method based on exact simulation techniques.
result: The MSTG method achieves super-exponential decay of truncation error and significantly reduces the integration dimension compared to standard EM scheme.
conclusion: The proposed approach greatly enhances practical efficiency of QMC for SDE simulation, as confirmed by numerical experiments.

title: Minimal Additive Codes And Additive Strong Blocking Sets
authors: Marine Le Meur Gianira N. Alfarano
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Additive codes over [MATH] generalize linear codes by relaxing linearity over the alphabet while retaining linearity over the subfield [MATH]. In this paper, we introduce minimal additive codes and we initiate their study from a geometric perspective. We define the concept of additive strong blocking sets, a class of [MATH]-projective systems whose union forms a strong blocking set. We establish a one-to-one correspondence between equivalence classes of nondegenerate minimal additive codes and equivalence classes of additive strong blocking sets. We also compare this framework with the theory of outer strong blocking sets, showing that the latter arises as a special case. Finally, we provide constructions and existence results for minimal additive codes, and derive upper, lower, and asymptotic bounds on their minimum length.
tldr: This paper introduces minimal additive codes and additive strong blocking sets, establishing a geometric correspondence between them.
motivation: To generalize minimal linear codes to additive codes over finite fields and study their geometric properties via strong blocking sets.
method: Defines additive strong blocking sets as projective systems whose union forms a strong blocking set, and proves a one-to-one correspondence with nondegenerate minimal additive codes.
result: Establishes equivalence between minimal additive codes and additive strong blocking sets, provides constructions, and derives bounds on minimum length.
conclusion: The framework generalizes outer strong blocking sets and offers new insights into additive codes from a geometric perspective.

title: Deep Numerical Schemes For Systems Of Ergodic BSDEs With Applications To Regime-switching Forward Utilities
authors: Guillaume Broux-Quemerais (LMM), Sarah Kaakai (LAGA), Anis Matoussi (LMM), Wissal Sabbagh
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce two neural-network-based numerical schemes for solving systems of coupled ergodic Backward Stochastic Differential Equations (eBSDEs), motivated by the approximation of optimal strategies within the framework of forward utilities in a regime-switching stochastic factor model. Our approach builds on the representation of such models through systems of eBSDEs introduced in [HLT20]. We first establish a link between the solution of the system of ergodic BSDEs and that of an associated multidimensional BSDE with random terminal time, given by the hitting time of the positive recurrent stochastic factor. Building on this representation, we introduce a locally additive deep learning scheme obtained by minimizing aggregated local error terms. We then present a new Deep Galerkin Method (DGM) inspired algorithm that minimizes the residual of the associated ergodic PDE system, relying on a representation of the ergodic cost. Finally, we apply this framework to regime-switching forward utilities in a stochastic factor model. We first derive a general consistency SPDE that characterizes regime-switching forward utilities and retrieve their representation with systems of ergodic BSDEs in the homothetic case. Numerical experiments demonstrate the performance of the proposed methods, with a particular focus on the impact on forward preferences of taking into account regime switches.
tldr: This paper introduces neural-network-based numerical schemes for solving systems of ergodic BSDEs with applications to regime-switching forward utilities in mathematical finance.
motivation: The authors aim to approximate optimal strategies in forward utility frameworks with regime-switching stochastic factors, which require solving systems of ergodic BSDEs that are analytically intractable.
method: Two deep learning schemes are proposed: one minimizes aggregated local error terms using a locally additive approach, and the other is a Deep Galerkin Method that minimizes the residual of the associated ergodic PDE system.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate the performance of the methods, particularly showing the impact of regime switches on forward preferences.
conclusion: The proposed neural-network schemes effectively solve ergodic BSDE systems and can be applied to regime-switching forward utility problems.

title: Extreme-Case Distorted Utility Under Moment Ambiguity
authors: Zehao Li, Yijie Peng, Hui Shao, Chung-Piaw Teo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many operations decisions under distributional ambiguity, from pricing and inventory to capacity and contracting, evaluate an action through a tail-sensitive distorted utility of an uncertain payoff and hedge against the least favorable distribution consistent with a few known moments; the resulting worst-case evaluation is the inner problem of a moment-based distributionally robust decision. We study this inner problem, the extreme-case distorted utility under moment constraints, for a locally Lipschitz utility that may be nonsmooth and neither convex nor concave together with a general, possibly atomic, distortion. Recasting the problem in the quantile domain, we develop a unified method that yields exact first-order optimality conditions and closed-form extremal values and distributions for both the worst and best cases, drawing on nonsmooth variational analysis. A central step treats the monotonicity constraint by isotonic projection onto the monotone cone, turning an abstract infinite-dimensional restriction into an inexpensive inner solve that scales linearly in the discretization. The method recovers and extends classical moment bounds through three examples: a range value-at-risk extension of the Scarf bound, GlueVaR distortions with a reward--penalty utility, and a capped incentive contract under conditional value-at-risk. As the inner oracle of a robust min-max decision, the characterization embeds directly in outer robust optimization, illustrated on a real capacity-provisioning problem for generative artificial intelligence inference where accounting for moment ambiguity lowers required capacity while preserving service compliance.
tldr: This paper studies worst-case distorted utility under moment ambiguity for operations decisions, using nonsmooth variational analysis and isotonic projection.
motivation: Operations decisions under distributional ambiguity require evaluating tail-sensitive distorted utilities against the least favorable distribution consistent with known moments.
method: The problem is recast in the quantile domain and solved via nonsmooth variational analysis, with monotonicity constraints handled by isotonic projection onto the monotone cone.
result: Exact first-order optimality conditions and closed-form extremal values and distributions are derived for both worst and best cases, recovering and extending classical moment bounds.
conclusion: The characterization serves as an inner oracle for robust min-max decisions, demonstrated on a capacity-provisioning problem for generative AI inference.

title: The 3d Nonconforming Virtual Element Method With Enhanced Spaces: Numerical Investigation And Implementation Guide
authors: Manuel Trezzi Franco Dassi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we describe the 3D Nonconforming Virtual Element Method, where the local spaces are enhanced in order to build an [MATH] projection of virtual functions onto polynomials of degree [MATH]. This higher order projection provides a more accurate representation of the load term and, more importantly, it enables the construction of the reaction term. We conduct a convergence analysis of the [MATH] norm and [MATH] seminorm errors with respect to mesh size and approximation degree. We also compare our results with those obtained using the conforming Virtual Element Method.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical investigation of the 3D nonconforming virtual element method with enhanced spaces for improved projection accuracy.
motivation: To improve the accuracy of the virtual element method for 3D problems by enhancing local spaces to better represent load and reaction terms.
method: The authors enhance the local virtual element spaces to enable a higher-order projection onto polynomials, and conduct convergence analysis in the H1 norm and H1 seminorm.
result: Convergence rates are analyzed with respect to mesh size and approximation degree, and comparisons are made with the conforming virtual element method.
conclusion: The enhanced nonconforming virtual element method shows improved accuracy and is a viable alternative to conforming methods for 3D problems.

title: A Multi-objective Perspective On Block-structured Integer Programs With One Soft Coupling Constraint
authors: Mark Lyngesen, Kathrin Klamroth, Britta Efkes, Sune Lauth Gadegaard
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a multi-objective perspective on block-structured integer programs featuring a single soft coupling constraint. By interpreting the coupling constraint as a second objective, we transform the coupled single-objective problem into an additively-separable bi-objective optimization problem. To avoid the expensive computation of the full Pareto front, we introduce an algorithm, which uses a binary search to isolate a region of interest around the soft constraint limit. This algorithm provides provable bounds on the single-objective optimum. We further enhance this algorithm, by exploiting the block-structure, using a novel [MATH]-lookup mechanism to skip repeated sub-problem calculations. Finally, for scenarios requiring all non-dominated solutions within the region of interest, we propose a new approach, that works its way from the middle of the region of interest outwards. This algorithm shows quick convergence in terms of representation. Computational studies demonstrate that our methods dramatically reduce integer programming calls, thereby outperforming traditional dichotomic search. For large instances the method works as a strong heuristic providing bounds on the gap to an optimal solution, providing trade-off information in addition to the solution.
tldr: This paper presents a multi-objective optimization approach for block-structured integer programs with a soft coupling constraint, using binary search and Pareto front techniques.
motivation: Solving block-structured integer programs with a coupling constraint is computationally expensive; the authors aim to reduce the number of integer programming calls by reformulating the problem as a bi-objective optimization.
method: The coupling constraint is treated as a second objective, transforming the problem into an additively-separable bi-objective problem. A binary search isolates a region of interest around the soft constraint limit, and a lookup mechanism skips repeated sub-problem calculations.
result: The proposed methods dramatically reduce integer programming calls compared to traditional dichotomic search, and for large instances they provide strong heuristic bounds with trade-off information.
conclusion: The multi-objective perspective offers an efficient way to handle block-structured integer programs with soft coupling constraints, providing both exact and heuristic solutions.

title: Explicit Confidence Bands And Intervals For Distribution Functions And Their Derivatives Via Random Weierstrass-type Operators
authors: Jos\'e A. Adell, J. T. Alcal\'a, C. Sang\"uesa
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical kernel estimators of second order are interpreted in terms of random Weierstrass-type operators, particularly random Steklov operators. This leads us to obtain explicit nonasymptotic confidence bands and intervals for distribution functions [MATH] and their derivatives [MATH]. Under the only assumption that [MATH] is uniformly continuous, confidence bands for [MATH] are established by using the Dvoretzky-Kiefer-Wolfowitz inequality. To give confidence intervals, we allow [MATH] to have isolated discontinuities of the first kind, so that we really estimate the midpoint function [MATH]. The proofs are based either on concentration inequalities for subordinated stochastic processes or accurate estimates of the MSE of the corresponding estimators. The length of the confidence bands and intervals depends on the degree of smoothness of [MATH] measured in terms of the second modulus of continuity. Both lengths are of order [MATH] if [MATH] is locally a polynomial of degree [MATH] at most.
tldr: The paper develops explicit nonasymptotic confidence bands and intervals for distribution functions and their derivatives using random Weierstrass-type operators.
motivation: To provide explicit, nonasymptotic confidence bands and intervals for distribution functions and their derivatives under minimal smoothness assumptions.
method: Interprets classical kernel estimators as random Weierstrass-type operators (e.g., random Steklov operators) and uses concentration inequalities and MSE estimates.
result: Obtains explicit confidence bands and intervals whose lengths depend on the second modulus of continuity, achieving order n^{-1/2} if the function is locally a polynomial of degree at most 1.
conclusion: The approach yields practical, nonasymptotic uncertainty quantification for distribution functions and their derivatives with only uniform continuity required.

title: Line Planning At Scale: Models, Methods And Insights
authors: Bart van Rossum Rolf van Lieshout
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24386v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Line planning, the problem of deciding which lines to operate and at what frequency, is a fundamental step in public transport planning. To accurately model passenger routing, the problem is traditionally defined on a change-and-go network (CGN), which captures transfers between lines exactly. However, this network grows large quickly and is hard to solve at scale. We compare the CGN against three more compact models, differing with respect to how transfers are approximated, and characterize how they relate in terms of solution quality and modeling accuracy. We develop state-of-the-art solution methods tailored to each model, and evaluate all four across 972 instances based on the Dutch and Swiss railway networks. Contrary to the CGN's canonical status, we find that it is competitive only on small or easy instances and often fails to find any feasible solution on large networks. Instead, a compact direct connection model performs best overall, finding the best solution on over 83\% of instances. Our results indicate that carefully designed approximations, rather than exact transfer modeling, are the more promising foundation for large-scale line planning.
tldr: This paper compares models and solution methods for line planning in public transport networks, finding that a compact direct connection model outperforms the traditional change-and-go network at scale.
motivation: Line planning is a fundamental step in public transport planning, but exact models become intractable for large networks. The paper aims to identify more scalable modeling approaches.
method: The authors compare four models (change-and-go network and three compact approximations) on 972 instances based on Dutch and Swiss railway networks, using state-of-the-art solution methods tailored to each.
result: The change-and-go network is only competitive on small instances, while a compact direct connection model finds the best solution on over 83% of instances.
conclusion: Carefully designed approximations are more promising than exact transfer modeling for large-scale line planning.

title: A Sparse Spectral Method On A Class Of Domains Bounded By Planar Algebraic Curves
authors: Jiajie Yao, Marco Fasondini, Sheehan Olver
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a sparse spectral method for solving partial differential equations on a class of two-dimensional geometries bounded by algebraic curves. The numerical method uses generalised bivariate Koornwinder polynomials which form a complete orthogonal basis, but one which is not graded in terms of polynomial degree. The polynomials are built from new families of univariate semiclassical orthogonal polynomials whose associated operator matrices (Jacobi matrices, raising matrices and differentiation matrices) are computed with optimal linear complexity in the number of basis functions. When used to discretise partial differential equations the resulting matrices are sparse enabling efficient numerical solution. Moreover, we develop fast transforms from values on a grid to expansion coefficients. The efficiency and accuracy of the resulting spectral method are illustrated through a series of numerical experiments on geometries whose boundaries are smooth and piecewise smooth including non-convex geometries. We observe algebraic convergence for geometries with corners, which accelerates to exponentially fast (spectral) convergence when the boundary is smooth.
tldr: This paper develops a sparse spectral method for solving PDEs on domains bounded by algebraic curves using generalized Koornwinder polynomials.
motivation: Efficient numerical solution of PDEs on complex geometries is important for many applications, but existing methods may be computationally expensive or lack sparsity.
method: The method uses bivariate Koornwinder polynomials built from new univariate semiclassical orthogonal polynomials, with Jacobi, raising, and differentiation matrices computed in optimal linear complexity, leading to sparse discretization matrices.
result: Numerical experiments show algebraic convergence for domains with corners and exponential (spectral) convergence for smooth boundaries, with efficient transforms from grid values to coefficients.
conclusion: The proposed sparse spectral method is efficient and accurate for solving PDEs on a class of algebraic-curve-bounded domains, offering a practical numerical tool.

title: Trade-off Invariance For Weighted Scalarizations In Multi-objective Optimization
authors: Alessandro Scagliotti Jona Klemenc
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider weighted-sum scalarizations for an abstract multi-objective minimization problem defined by the vector-valued map [MATH], where [MATH] is an arbitrary nonempty set and no topology, convexity, compactness, or lower semicontinuity assumption is imposed. Using the open simplex as parameter space for positive weights, we show that the Trade-off Invariance Principle for scalarizations yields a generic uniqueness property in the objective space. Namely, for almost every weight vector, all minimizers of the corresponding weighted-sum scalarization have the same objective vector. Moreover, excluding again a null-measure subset, all minimizing sequences determine the same limiting objective vector, independently of the chosen sequence. We also give a geometric interpretation of these results in the attainable objective set: for almost every positive weight vector, the scalarization exposes at most one nondominated point. Moreover, minimizing sequences determine at most one asymptotically exposed objective vector in the closure of the attainable set.
tldr: This paper proves a trade-off invariance principle for weighted-sum scalarizations in abstract multi-objective optimization, showing generic uniqueness of minimizers and limiting objective vectors.
motivation: Multi-objective optimization often uses weighted-sum scalarizations, but the relationship between weight vectors and the set of minimizers is not well understood in a general setting without topological or convexity assumptions.
method: The authors consider an abstract minimization problem with a vector-valued map and use the open simplex as parameter space for positive weights. They apply the Trade-off Invariance Principle to derive generic properties of minimizers and minimizing sequences.
result: For almost every weight vector, all minimizers of the weighted-sum scalarization have the same objective vector, and all minimizing sequences determine the same limiting objective vector, independent of the sequence.
conclusion: The results provide a geometric interpretation: for almost every positive weight vector, the scalarization exposes at most one nondominated point, and minimizing sequences determine at most one asymptotically exposed objective vector in the closure of the attainable set.

title: Ferguson's Dirichlet Process Breakthrough: A Lasting Legacy
authors: Antonio Lijoi, Igor Pruenster, Junyi Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ferguson's 1973 introduction of the Dirichlet process marked a breakthrough in Bayesian nonparametric statistics. For the first time, a prior on the space of probability measures fulfilled two key desiderata: large support and analytical tractability. In this paper, we review three complementary constructions of the Dirichlet process, whose roots can be traced back to Ferguson: through finite-dimensional distributions, via normalization of a gamma process, and through predictive distributions. Each perspective not only deepens the understanding of the Dirichlet process but also provides a template for generalizations, from normalized random measures with independent increments to Gibbs--type priors and beyond. Over the past fifty years, the Dirichlet process has become the cornerstone of Bayesian nonparametric methodology and applications, while simultaneously inspiring the expansion of the landscape of nonparametric priors. Since de Finetti laid out the Bayesian nonparametric framework in the 1930s, the key obstacle had been the absence of a tractable nonparametric prior. Ferguson's contribution overcame this challenge, providing a solution to a decades-long open problem. In recognition of this decisive advance, it seems appropriate to refer to the Dirichlet process as the Ferguson--Dirichlet process.
tldr: This paper reviews the Dirichlet process in Bayesian nonparametric statistics, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The Dirichlet process is a foundational prior in Bayesian nonparametrics, but the paper has no connection to the user's research interests.
method: The paper reviews three constructions of the Dirichlet process: via finite-dimensional distributions, normalization of a gamma process, and predictive distributions.
result: It highlights the Dirichlet process as a cornerstone of Bayesian nonparametric methodology and its generalizations.
conclusion: The Dirichlet process, proposed by Ferguson, solved a long-standing problem in Bayesian nonparametrics and remains influential.

title: Rigidity Of McMullen Julia Sets
authors: Yan Gao, Luxian Yang, Jinsong Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a complete quasisymmetric classification of the Julia sets of postcritically finite McMullen maps [MATH] with [MATH] and [MATH], and prove that the quasisymmetry group of each such Julia set is exactly the finite dihedral group generated by the natural symmetries of the map. These results establish quasisymmetric rigidity for all topological classes in this family, including Sierpi\'{n}ski-like carpets, necklaces, and clusters, and provide the first known examples of rigid Julia sets in each of the three classes.
tldr: This paper classifies Julia sets of postcritically finite McMullen maps and proves quasisymmetric rigidity.
motivation: To understand the quasisymmetric geometry of Julia sets arising from a specific family of rational maps.
method: Using complex dynamics and quasisymmetric geometry techniques to analyze topological classes of Julia sets.
result: Complete quasisymmetric classification and proof that the quasisymmetry group is a finite dihedral group.
conclusion: These Julia sets are rigid, providing the first examples of rigid Julia sets in Sierpiński-like carpets, necklaces, and clusters.

title: Variational Convexity: New Characterizations, Calculus Rules, And Applications
authors: Ziyuan Wang Radu Ioan Bot
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Introduced by R.T. Rockafellar in 2019, variational convexity is a generalized notion of convexity under which stationary points of nonconvex optimization problems can still be guaranteed to exhibit local optimality. In this paper, we provide characterizations of variationally convex functions through their proximal hulls and epigraphs, and investigate operations that preserve variational convexity, including nonlinear and linear composition, summation, and proximal averaging.
